1.why: The system enforces server-side authorization by verifying challenge ownership (identityKey and accountId) and constant-time code comparison before issuing a session.

2.why: The same verification code does not work for any other user; each challenge is tied to a specific identityKey and accountId.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated (deleted) when a new session is created after MFA enablement.

4.why: OTP shared secret is encrypted (AES-GCM) and backup codes are hashed (PBKDF2) before storage.

5.why: Secrets and codes are generated using crypto.getRandomValues() (cryptographically secure RNG).

6.why: Secrets, OTPs, and session tokens are stored in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies or server-side only.

7.why: Server-side input validation is performed for email, phone, OTP, and recovery codes (e.g., emailOK, phoneOK, otpOK, recoveryInput).

8.why: Contextual output encoding is applied in the HTML template (e.g., nonce-based CSP, escaped dynamic content in the page).

9.why: Redirects are restricted to an allow-list (ROUTES) of internal paths, with no open redirects.

10.why: Secure headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors) are set in secureHeaders().

11.why: Session cookies are set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: OTP seeds, backup codes, and session tokens are never exposed in logs, URLs, or error output; stack traces are suppressed.

13.why: Verification codes (OTP) are single-use (marked as used after validation) and time-bound (CHALLENGE_MS expiry).

14.why: Repeated failed attempts are rate-limited (MAX_FAILURES) and locked out (LOCK_MS) for identity, OTP, and recovery attempts.

15.why: Session identifier is rotated on authentication (new token generated), has idle/absolute timeouts, and is invalidated on logout.
